header: Date: 2027-07-27 | Start: 10:00 AM EDT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (RiverMark CTO), Sana Patel (Platform Eng), Mark Donovan (SRE)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review latency tuning experiments. Covered TTFT improvements with streaming, impact of sequence length and kernel selection on p50/p95, and initial Dedicated capacity pricing. Agreed next steps for more exhaustive benchmarks and security scoping.
topics: kernel choice A vs B (optimized matmul kernels)
sequence length distribution and batching tradeoffs
KV cache and prefix caching benefits
Dedicated vs Hosted capacity and pricing
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — review last weeks runs, streaming, kernels, next steps. can everyone hear me ok?
[00:06] Alex: yes good here, thanks Jordan.
[00:10] Priya: hey yep, all good. i've got the slides up but i'll just talk through the numbers we ran.
[00:15] Sana: joining from home - slight echo but okay.
[00:20] Priya: cool. so we re-ran the 1k sample with the 7b q4 model, baseline was non-streaming, kernel set A. baseline TTFT median ~120ms, p50 generation latency ~220ms for 64-token prompts, p95 around 650ms for 512 token sequences.
[00:38] Mark: can you clarify TTFT here? is that client to first token after auth?
[00:42] Priya: yeah, TTFT measured from request received at our edge to first token returned to client socket. includes routing and model warm-up when necessary.
[00:50] Jordan: and you called out kernel A; we also tested kernel B which is more optimized for longer sequences, right?
[00:56] Priya: exactly. kernel A is our general-purpose kernel set, kernel B has attention tiling and better fused kernels for matmul at longer seq lengths. on the same tests kernel B dropped p95 from 650ms to ~420ms for 512 tokens. p50 also improved but less dramatically.
[01:12] Alex: nice. did you have to change batch size or kv settings?
[01:16] Priya: we kept batch size at 1 for TTFT-focused runs. we also enabled prefix KV cache for repeated conversation cases, which helped for subsequent requests (p50 down by ~30% on repeated prefixes).
[01:28] Sana: what about streaming? we heard that streaming can reduce perceived latency a lot.
[01:31] Priya: yes — we enabled streaming (chunked token send) and TTFT dropped from 120ms median to about 45-55ms median because we can send the first token earlier while backend continues generation. p95 improved somewhat but depends on sequence length because if long sequences, backend still takes time to fill later tokens.
[01:50] Mark: is the streaming improvement mostly network/transport or kernel related?
[01:54] Priya: mostly architectural — streaming overlaps compute+network; it hides tail latency of full completion. also helps when kernels have progressive token emission. but kernel choice still impacts throughput and p95 for long tails.
[02:06] Jordan: customers often care about TTFT for chat UX; sounds like streaming should be enabled by default for RiverMark's use case. Alex, is that accurate?
[02:14] Alex: yes, for our agent experience TTFT is critical. some endpoints are short responses (20-50 tokens), others are long (up to 1k). we need both.
[02:24] Priya: that split matters — we recommended route-level config: streaming on chat endpoints, non-streaming for batch synth jobs.
[02:31] Sana: good idea. what about sequence length distribution — we pulled a histogram: 60% requests < 128 tokens, 30% 128-512, 10% >512.
[02:42] Priya: that matches our tuning guidance. given that, kernel B helps on the 40% mid-to-long tail, but kernel A is slightly better for short sequences in single-token TTFT. there's a small tradeoff.
[02:55] Mark: any quantization impacts? we saw a slight quality delta when going to q4_0 in our dev tests.
[03:01] Priya: quantization (q4) reduces memory and improves throughput, but affects logits slightly. our internal eval shows small precision differences but for many generative tasks it's acceptable. we can run an eval on your prompt set to measure regressions.
[03:13] Alex: yes please — that will determine whether we accept q4 in production.
[03:17] Jordan: note for pricing — q4 on Dedicated changes GPU packing and costs, we'll include that in the Dedicated pricing doc.
[03:24] Sana: speaking of Dedicated, what latency SLOs did you target?
[03:27] Priya: for Dedicated reserved 2x capacity we can target p95 under 600ms for 512-token typical workloads with kernel B and streaming for chat. TTFT under 80ms median for chat streaming.
[03:39] Alex: ok that's close to our internal target of 500ms p95 for interactive flows. can you bump numbers?
[03:45] Jordan: we can run a follow-up with more nodes or different instance type — we'll include recommendations.
[03:50] Priya: also worth noting batching — for throughput cost reduction, batching helps but increases TTFT if you wait to fill a batch. we support dynamic batching with latency SLOs: small idle timeout to collect a micro-batch (10-20ms) which keeps TTFT reasonable while gaining some amortization.
[04:08] Mark: do you have results for batch sizes 4?
[04:11] Priya: yes briefly: batch=4 for short sequences improved tokens/sec by ~2.2x but TTFT increased by ~30ms median. it's a tradeoff.
[04:19] Alex: what's the recommended default?
[04:21] Priya: for your workload given 60% short we recommend batching disabled for chat endpoints and enabled for async batch jobs. for mixed endpoints, route-based policies are best.
[04:31] Sana: back to kernels — how do you pick kernel at runtime? automatic?
[04:35] Priya: runtime does kernel selection based on seq length profile and model shape; we also allow pinning. for the POC we tried auto-select and pinned kernel B for the long-test group. auto-select worked but pinned gives consistent behavior for benchmarking.
[04:50] Alex: curious if kernel switching causes any cold-starts or cache warming issues?
[04:54] Priya: switching kernels typically requires process restart if it's a fundamentally different binary, so we prefer one kernel per serving pool. auto-select chooses pool based on incoming request characteristics, so no frequent restarts.
[05:07] Jordan: security quick check — Alex, any new asks?
[05:10] Alex: we need SOC2 scope confirmation and SSO integration details. also, can Redwood's audit logs show token-level cost breakdown per route?
[05:18] Jordan: yes audit logs show per-request metadata and token counts; we can map tokens to routes for cost breakdowns. we'll attach the security pack.
[05:25] Sana: for VPC/on-prem — we may need a private deployment later; currently testing Hosted but will likely move to Private for regulated flows.
[05:33] Priya: we recommended a staged approach: start Hosted, run pilot, then migrate hot paths to Dedicated or Private while keeping non-sensitive analytic workloads on Hosted.
[05:42] Mark: any constraints around KMS/HSM?
[05:45] Jordan: Dedicated and Private both support customer-managed KMS; Private supports HSM integrations. we'll include that in the security doc.
[05:53] Alex: great. can you also share a one-page cheat sheet on tuning knobs (streaming, batch timeout, kernel pinning, kv cache) we can hand to our infra team?
[06:02] Priya: yes, will include that as a follow-up.
[06:06] Jordan: ok, let's quickly walk through the detailed numbers in the spreadsheet Priya shared — Priya go ahead.
[06:12] Priya: right. slide 1: baseline numbers (non-streaming, kernel A) TTFT median 120ms. slide 2: streaming enabled TTFT median 50ms, end-to-end p95 improved 10-20% for short sequences. slide 3: kernel B results: p95 for 512 tokens 650ms -> 420ms, CPU GPU utilization dropped about 12% for same throughput.
[06:40] Mark: did you run the kernel B test with different CUDA/cuDNN versions? we saw slight perf shifts depending on driver.
[06:46] Priya: tests ran on our recommended driver stack (CUDA 12.1, cuDNN 9.x), we can re-run on your infra if you share driver/instance info.
[06:55] Alex: we'll share our instance types — mostly G5a-like and a few A10n.
[07:00] Priya: noted. next, slide 4: batching impact — for batchsize 4 throughput improved but TTFT increased. slide 5: kv cache results — when prefix cache hit, subsequent requests saw 30-40% latency reduction depending on prefix reuse.
[07:19] Sana: what about memory pressure with kv cache for long contexts?
[07:23] Priya: KV cache memory grows with context length; we recommend TTL on cache entries and eviction policy for heavy tail sequences. Dedicated gives more predictable memory headroom.
[07:33] Alex: are there any fallback policies we should configure if Dedicated pool hits capacity?
[07:37] Priya: yes, smart routing supports fallback to hosted or cheaper model variants. policy can be region-aware and cost-aware. we recommend configuring hard capacity alerts plus soft-fallback thresholds.
[07:49] Mark: ok. any surprises in the runs?
[07:52] Priya: only one: on a small subset we saw jitter spikes tied to GC pauses in the runtime when we enabled a debug tracing flag — that was my fault, disabled now.
[07:59] Jordan: classic. thanks for catching.
[08:02] Alex: timeline — we want to sign pilot go-live by mid-August if tests look good. possible?
[08:08] Jordan: yes, if we get the 1k streaming + kernel runs and your sample traces in the next week we'll have a pilot plan.
[08:14] Priya: i'll run the A/B kernels with streaming and non-streaming and share raw CSVs.
[08:19] Sana: please include raw latency histograms and sample traces.
[08:22] Priya: will do.
[08:24] Jordan: last piece — pricing: i'll send Dedicated 2x reserved estimate; includes estimated token costs and infra margin.
[08:31] Alex: ok. any blockers on our side?
[08:34] Sana: just security scoping and our internal procurement timelines.
[08:37] Jordan: we'll align on security Qs and pricing this week.
[08:40] Mark: can we get a demo of the console for tracing and per-route latency breakdown?
[08:44] Priya: yes we can schedule a short demo next week.
[08:47] Jordan: great. recap of action items... Priya to run A/B, Jordan pricing and security pack, Alex to share traces.
[08:56] Alex: sounds good. thanks all.
[09:00] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links and next steps. bye.
